content.text:
Entire Explain:

Enchanting is a two-step system:

1. Gather reagents and gold.
2. Use an enchanting bench to craft a scroll, then apply that scroll to compatible gear.

The main definitions live in [enchantCatalog.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/content/enchanting/enchantCatalog.js:1), and the crafting flow is implemented in [benchGame.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/content/enchanting/benchGame.js:71).

### Craftable scrolls

- Venom Binding — weapon; poison proc. Costs spider legs, venom gland, resin, and 65 gold.
- Firestorm Binding — weapon; lingering fire proc. Costs ember root, ashes, oil, rune fragment, and 70 gold.
- Frost Binding — weapon; frost proc. Costs moonleaf, water, frost core, rune fragment, and 70 gold.
- Flame Ward — armor/accessories/offhand/ranged; passive fire resistance. Costs ashes, resin, ember root, bone dust, and 80 gold.
- Venom Ward — armor/accessories/offhand/ranged; passive poison resistance. Costs venom fronds, venom gland, cursed thread, and 80 gold.
- Fortified Binding — armor/accessories/offhand/ranged; passive impact resistance. Costs resin, beast claw, bone dust, and 75 gold.

Crafting is deterministic: if you have the requirements, the materials and gold are consumed and the scroll is placed in your inventory. There is no crafting success roll.

### Applying a scroll

Apply the scroll to an eligible item from your inventory or equipped gear. The scroll is consumed only after a successful application.

The enchant is persistent on the item and is represented by an affix such as `firestorm1` or `fireWard1`. The game also creates runtime enchantment topology beneath the item so combat systems can evaluate its effects. The same enchant cannot be applied twice; an invalid target or duplicate leaves the scroll intact.

Slot rules normalize `ring1`/`ring2` to rings and `shield` to offhand. Ammunition cannot be enchanted.

### Gems are a second enchantment-like system

Real socketable gems can be applied to items with open sockets. Gems provide both a passive bonus and usually an on-hit proc. Examples:

- Ruby: fire resistance and a chance to ignite.
- Emerald: poison resistance and a chance to poison.
- Diamond: attack/defense bonuses and bonus physical damage.
- Voidstone: attack/damage bonuses and a chance to drain HP.
- Fluorite: electrical resistance and a charge-based lightning discharge.

Socketing consumes the gem and attaches a `GemSocketNode` runtime subtree to the item. Fluorite is the unusual one: electric damage gives it charges, and at 3+ charges the next hit releases bonus electric damage and blinds the target. See [gems.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/data/gems.js:81) and [gemSocketAffixes.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/data/gemSocketAffixes.js:61).

In play, the intended loop is: visit the Enchantress, collect monster- and environment-themed reagents, craft the scroll you want, apply it to suitable equipment, and use the Gem Vendor/socket system for additional build customization.

Recorded intent was not available for the relevant enchanting commits—the commits have no Entire checkpoint trailers—so the implementation details above are verified from current source and tests rather than session transcripts.
